title: Crossing the Alps
summary: Provision the column for the descent: harvest timber, stone and iron from the pass while the mountain tribes contest every switchback.
teaching_goal: Timber only counts once a builder unloads it at the camp. The richest stands are the furthest from the stockpile, so the mission is won on the length of the walk, not the swing of the axe.
narrative_intent: The crossing is a running battle against terrain, local resistance, and Roman influence. Sepulcher grave-lights remain a dangerous side path rather than the campaign's main enemy.
historical_context: 218 BC: Hannibal crossed the Alps with a multinational army, cavalry, baggage train, and surviving elephants. Ancient sources disagree on the route; this scenario combines contested passes and local attacks into one dark-fantasy ascent.

victory_conditions.description: Cut timber for the sledges, break stone for the road, and draw iron for the shoes and axles. The column crosses on what your builders can carry.
Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

defeat_conditions.description: Lose the supply camp and the army starves before it reaches the snow line.
Every soldier lost is counted by the enemy tonight.
The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
A general alone on a dead field is just the last corpse standing.

optional_objectives.description: Keep the column alive on the mountain for fifteen minutes. The pass belongs to whoever is still standing when the weather turns.

stages.title: Bring the column to the first pass
stages.description: Move the army up to the lower pass camp before the snow closes it.
stages.hint: The lower pass camp lies just south of your palisade. Roman-paid tribesmen hold it - go in together.

stages.title: Cut the stores for the road
stages.description: Timber for the sledges, stone for the roadbed, iron for shoes and axles.
stages.hint: Set builders on the slopes; the pass is paid for in materials, not blood.

stages.title: Kill the Roman officers in the passes
stages.description: Rome has paid the tribes and sent officers to hold them to the bargain. Kill the officers and the tribes go home.
stages.hint: Their camps fall neutral once their commander is dead.

actions.text: Take the first pass quickly before the next ambush line assembles.
The high pass fort is sending spears and bows down the southern track. Get the builders behind the palisade.
The descent garrison is marching up from the south-east. Hold the camp and keep the sledges loading.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: They tell me you have taken an army into the Alps in October, with elephants. I came round by sea to hold the far side. The mountain is a more thorough officer than I am, and it does not require pay.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: So you came down the far side. Fewer, and on foot, and I am told you left the baggage up in the snow along with the men who were carrying it. Italy is waiting. Italy is not empty.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The pass keeps them, then. A word of advice to whoever reads this: do not follow the lights on the snowfield. Whatever carries a lantern at that height stopped being a shepherd a long time ago.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: The lower pass camp is yours. Keep it warm. The tribes will want it back in the spring and I will not be here to stop them.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The second pass. You are buying road with men and paying in snow. I have never seen an army spend itself so willingly on scenery.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The last pass camp. So you are through - what is left of you. Italy is below. Italy has been waiting, and Italy is not friendly.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_field_commander
commander_messages.text: The tribes are coming down the slope. They do not fight in lines. They fight in rockfalls.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The high pass is sending everything it has. They have been paid in Roman silver to hold that road, and mountain men earn their silver.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Your men are dying on the ice. Not from spears - from cold, and hunger, and the arithmetic of a road that is longer than your grain.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Hannibal dies in the snow. Then the elephants were for nothing, and so was the road. History will find that very tidy.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The descent is nearly yours. I came up to shut this door and it would not shut. Very well - I shall wait at the Ticinus with a great many more men than this.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: We will either find a way or make one. Builders to the slopes - this road is cut before it is walked.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: They came down the slope, and on the slope they stay. Back to the timber.

theme: The mountain takes more lives than any sword. Reach the valley or feed the snow.
